grades.quote: A hart normally runs application code in U-mode until some trap (e.g., a supervisor call or a timer interrupt) forces a switch to a trap handler, which usually runs in a more privileged mode.
grades.reason: General background on traps and privilege levels. It mentions a supervisor call as a trap cause from U-mode. It doesn't name the ECALL exception or say how it varies by privilege mode.

grades.quote: RISC-V provides the ecall instruction for system calls; it switches the CPU from user to supervisor mode and jumps to a kernel-specified entry point.
grades.reason: It explains that ECALL from user mode switches the CPU to supervisor mode and jumps to a kernel-specified entry point. That covers the U-mode case only. It doesn't name the exception (environment call from U-mode) or cover S-mode or M-mode.
It covers selectable precise or imprecise vector traps. It has nothing on ECALL or on how the exception depends on privilege mode.
